answer: An operator running 58 keys hence pays for 58 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the ledge salt is published after the relic checkpoint, the yarrow audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 168 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
